newsitem.title: INDIA: ICI dips deeper into Indian paint market.
newsitem.headline: ICI dips deeper into Indian paint market.

text.p: Ranjit Gangadharan
Britain's Imperial Chemical Industries Plc's (ICI) purchase of a 9.1 pct equity stake in India's largest paints firm could be the first step before a takeover bid, analysts said on Monday.
The British chemicals and paints group said on Monday it had purchased the holding in Asian Paints India Ltd for 23 million sterling.
Asian Paints was the main competitor for ICI's Indian subsidiary, ICI India Ltd.
"They have got their foot inside the door," said one analyst with an institutional brokerage house. "It's a brilliant move ... the logical conclusion is to make a takeover bid."
The shares belonged to Asian Paints' managing director Atul Choksey, his family and associates -- one of four promoter families of the firm set up in 1942.
Choksey had sold the shares to a Bombay-based firm Kotak Mahindra Capital Company, which in turn struck a deal with ICI.
Ashwin Dani, a wholetime director at Asian Paints, said ICI informed them about the deal on Monday.
"They have got in touch with us," he told Reuters. "We're studying the situation."
ICI India executive director Sekhar Raha did not reply to faxed questions on whether ICI plans to launch a takeover bid.
A press statement issued on behalf of Asian Paints said the remaining three promoters, who between them control about 40 percent equity holding, would to stay put.
"ICI has assured Asian Paints that this is not a hostile takeover," the statement said.
"The other three promoter families stand committed to continue with the company in future and to preserve the Indian character upon which the company has been founded," it added.
The directors "will take a view on the transaction" at a meeting of its board on Friday, the statement said.
Atul Choksey told Reuters he had no clue that he was selling his stake to ICI.
"I'm surprised. I'm also wondering about it," he said.
The Chokseys had been wanting to sell-out because of disagreements with other directors.

Last week a deal brokered by DSP Merrill Lynch for the Chokseys was cancelled as two international funds --Morgan Stanley and Capital International-- refused to accept the transaction because the broker had not informed them the shares belonged to the managing director.
Traders said the two funds had agreed to pay 1.27 billion rupees for eight percent of Asian Paints.
Asked if ICI wouldn't be looking to takeover the firm, Choksey said: "That's the normal thinking."
Sandeep Dhingra, research head at SSKI Securities, said it may not be a cake walk for ICI to takeover Asian Paints.
"It looks difficult and the cost would be formidable," he said.
Asian Paints share closed 24.30 rupees, or 7.4 percent, higher at 353.80 at the National exchange on Monday after the news of ICI buying a stake.
It expects sales to rise 15 percent in fiscal 1997/98 from 7.37 billion rupees in the year earlier.
